title: Journey on Mastering React Js
content:
Learning React has been quite an experience for me. Unlike structured courses or formal education, my journey has been shaped by self-learning through YouTube tutorials and extensive online research. It has been both challenging and rewarding, pushing me to explore beyond my comfort zone and truly understand how modern web applications function.

At first, React seemed intimidating. The concept of components, JSX, and state management felt overwhelming, especially coming from a traditional HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript background. I started with the basics, watching beginner-friendly YouTube tutorials that broke down the core concepts. These videos helped me understand the fundamental building blocks of React, such as functional and class components, props, and state. Seeing code written and explained in real-time made it easier to grasp the flow of a React application.

However, just watching videos was not enough. I quickly realized that passive learning would not get me far, so I began experimenting with the code on my own. I would pause the videos, replicate the examples, and modify them to see how React behaved. This hands-on approach made a huge difference. Whenever I encountered errors, I turned to Google, Stack Overflow, and the official React documentation to troubleshoot and deepen my understanding.

One of the biggest hurdles was state management. Understanding how state works within a component and how to efficiently pass data between components took me some time. I watched multiple tutorials explaining different state management techniques, from React’s built-in useState and useEffect hooks to more advanced solutions like Context API and Redux. The more I practiced, the clearer it became. Eventually, I built small projects to apply what I had learned, such as a to-do app and a weather dashboard.

Research played a crucial role in my learning process. Sometimes, YouTube tutorials didn’t provide all the answers, so I had to read blog posts, browse GitHub repositories, and follow discussions on developer forums. I also explored various best practices, such as optimizing performance, structuring a React project, and handling API calls efficiently. Each piece of information added another layer of understanding to my React knowledge.

One of the most valuable lessons I’ve learned so far is that learning React—or any technology—requires persistence and a willingness to solve problems independently. While YouTube and online resources provide guidance, true learning happens when I actively apply concepts, debug issues, and seek solutions on my own. This process has not only improved my React skills but also made me a more confident and resourceful developer.

Though my journey with React is far from over, I have already gained a solid foundation. As I continue building projects and exploring more advanced topics like Next.js, I look forward to refining my skills even further. This self-taught path has reinforced the idea that with enough curiosity and determination, learning anything is possible.

title: Building My First Project With API Integration
content:
Building DomConv, my currency converter web app, was an exciting journey filled with first-time experiences, endless debugging, and a deep dive into API documentation. This project tested my problem-solving skills and pushed me to become better at handling external APIs.

I wanted to build a simple yet functional currency converter that allows users to get real-time exchange rates for different currencies. The goal was to provide an intuitive and responsive interface where users could select currencies and instantly see the converted amount.

Since I needed live exchange rates, I researched different currency conversion APIs and decided on CurrencyAPI.com due to its reliability and ease of use. However, integrating an API for the first time was a challenge that required me to step out of my comfort zone.

Before writing any code, I had to go through the API documentation. Initially, it felt overwhelming, but I quickly realized that breaking it down into sections made it easier to understand. I learned about API endpoints, authentication using API keys, and how to make requests to fetch data.

I used HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to build the frontend. The layout consisted of a dropdown for selecting the base currency, a second dropdown for selecting the target currency, an input field for entering the amount, a button to trigger the conversion, and a section to display the converted amount. Styling was kept minimal yet user-friendly to ensure a seamless user experience.

After setting up the UI, the next step was making API calls using JavaScript. I encountered multiple challenges while working on this part, including understanding how to retrieve exchange rates and properly handling the data in my application.

While implementing the API, I faced several issues such as CORS errors, invalid API responses due to incorrect API keys or exceeded request limits, and handling network failures. Each challenge required careful debugging and research. I learned to use console logs, check API responses, and read error messages thoroughly to pinpoint issues.

After successfully implementing the API, I worked on optimizing the UI, adding loading indicators, and ensuring a smooth user experience. I also tested the app with different currencies to verify accuracy.

Throughout this project, I learned that reading documentation is crucial, debugging is an essential part of the process, and APIs are powerful tools that can greatly enhance user experience.

Going forward, I plan to add support for cryptocurrency conversions, implement a historical exchange rate feature, and enhance the UI with animations and a better design.

DomConv was a great learning experience, and I'm excited to build even more API-powered applications in the future. If you're new to APIs, my advice is: start small, read the docs, and don't be afraid to debug!

Would love to hear your thoughts! Let me know what features you'd like to see next on DomConv.

title: My Coding Journey: How It All Began
content:
My journey into coding started during the COVID-19 lockdown. With so much free time and nowhere to go, I decided to explore something new, and that’s when I discovered HTML. It was my first step into the world of programming, and even though it seemed simple at first, it opened the door to endless possibilities. I spent hours learning how to structure web pages, styling them with CSS, and adding a bit of interactivity with JavaScript.

After finishing secondary school, I knew I wanted to take my skills further, so I enrolled in a tech institute called Aptech. There, I was exposed to a structured learning environment that helped me understand the foundations of computer science and software development. While studying at Aptech, I realized that web development wasn’t just about frontend work—I needed to understand backend technologies too. That’s when I started learning Python for backend development through a private tutor. This experience deepened my understanding of how web applications work, from handling user data to setting up servers and databases.

As I progressed, I wanted to build more complex projects and bring my ideas to life. That’s when I discovered React. Transitioning from plain JavaScript to a framework like React was a challenge, but it was worth it. Learning about components, state management, and the power of reusable UI elements changed how I approached development. It wasn’t easy, and I often found myself stuck, but through continuous practice, watching tutorials, and working on real projects, I started getting comfortable with it.

Now, I am focused on building projects that not only showcase my skills but also solve real problems. Looking back, I can see how far I’ve come—from writing my first HTML tag to developing full-fledged applications with React and Python. The journey hasn’t been smooth, but every struggle and late-night debugging session has been a stepping stone toward becoming a better developer.

This is just the beginning. There’s still so much to learn, but I’m excited about what the future holds as I continue improving and expanding my knowledge in the world of programming.

title: Exploring Coding and Computer Science as a University Student
content:
Learning to code while being a university student is an adventure filled with late nights, constant struggles, and small victories that make it all worthwhile. Balancing coursework with personal coding projects is never easy, but the thrill of solving a problem after hours of debugging keeps me going.

Many nights, I find myself staring at my screen, trying to understand complex React concepts or figuring out why my JavaScript function isn't working as expected. React, in particular, has been a major challenge. While I understand the basics of HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, stepping into a framework like React feels like entering a whole new world. The component-based structure, state management, and hooks all seemed overwhelming at first, but with persistence and a lot of research, I am starting to get the hang of it.

YouTube has been my go-to learning resource. Watching tutorials, pausing, implementing code, and then debugging when things don’t work is my routine. However, I quickly realized that simply watching videos isn’t enough—I have to build projects and break things to truly understand how React works. That’s where the struggle begins.

Coding overnight has become a habit, not necessarily by choice, but because time feels different when I am deep into fixing bugs or learning a new concept. What starts as just one more fix often turns into hours of trial and error. There’s a unique kind of frustration that comes with spending hours on an issue only to realize the mistake was a missing semicolon or a wrongly named variable. But that frustration turns into excitement when everything finally works.

Despite the struggles, there’s something incredibly rewarding about learning new technologies and seeing my progress. Looking back, I remember when even writing a simple function seemed difficult. Now, I can build dynamic web applications, handle APIs, and slowly but surely understand how everything connects.

The journey is tough, but I wouldn't trade it for anything. Coding has taught me patience, persistence, and problem-solving in ways that traditional coursework never could. I know the road ahead is still long, and there’s so much more to learn, but every struggle is a step closer to mastering this skill. For now, I’ll keep pushing through, one bug at a time.
